subject: chemistry
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What is the chemical symbol for sodium?
questions.explain: Sodium's symbol Na comes from its Latin name natrium.

questions.q: What is the chemical symbol for potassium?
questions.explain: Potassium's symbol K comes from its Latin name kalium.

questions.q: What is the chemical symbol for iron?
questions.explain: Iron's symbol Fe comes from its Latin name ferrum.

questions.q: What is the chemical formula of magnesium oxide?
questions.explain: Magnesium (valency 2) and oxygen (valency 2) combine in a 1:1 ratio to give MgO.

questions.q: Using valencies, what is the correct formula of calcium chloride?
questions.explain: Calcium has a valency of 2 and chlorine a valency of 1, so two chloride ions balance one calcium ion.

questions.q: What is the correct formula of aluminium oxide?
questions.explain: Aluminium (valency 3) and oxygen (valency 2) cross over to give the ratio Al2O3.

questions.q: What is the valency (charge magnitude) of the sulfate ion, SO4?
questions.explain: The sulfate ion carries a 2- charge, so its valency is 2.

questions.q: What is the correct formula of aluminium sulfate?
questions.explain: Aluminium (valency 3) and sulfate (valency 2) combine so two Al balance three SO4 groups.

questions.q: Which state symbol is used to show a substance dissolved in water?
questions.explain: The symbol (aq) stands for aqueous, meaning dissolved in water.

questions.q: What does the state symbol (l) represent?
questions.explain: The symbol (l) indicates that a substance is in the liquid state.

questions.q: How should sodium chloride dissolved in water be written with a state symbol?
questions.explain: Dissolved in water means aqueous, so the symbol (aq) is used.

questions.q: Which is the balanced equation for the reaction of hydrogen with oxygen to form water?
questions.explain: This gives four H atoms and two O atoms on each side, so it is balanced.

questions.q: In a balanced chemical equation, what must be the same on both sides?
options: The number of atoms of each element
questions.explain: Atoms are neither created nor destroyed, so each element must have equal atoms on both sides.

questions.q: Balance the equation: Mg + O2 -> MgO
questions.explain: This balances two Mg and two O atoms on each side.

questions.q: Balance the equation for the Haber process: N2 + H2 -> NH3
questions.explain: This gives two N and six H atoms on each side, so it is balanced.

questions.q: What is the formula, including charge, of the ammonium ion?
questions.explain: The ammonium ion is NH4+, a positively charged polyatomic ion with a valency of 1.

questions.q: What is the chemical symbol for copper?
questions.explain: Copper's symbol Cu comes from its Latin name cuprum.

questions.q: What is the correct formula of sodium carbonate?
questions.explain: Sodium (valency 1) and carbonate (valency 2) combine so two Na balance one CO3 group.

questions.q: Which balanced equation correctly represents the thermal decomposition of calcium carbonate?
questions.explain: One CaCO3 gives one CaO and one CO2, with atoms balanced on both sides.

questions.q: What is the correct formula of iron(III) oxide?
questions.explain: Iron(III) has a valency of 3 and oxygen a valency of 2, giving the ratio Fe2O3.
